### 17.4 Why the index is not capnp, and why that could change

The workspace rule is *use capnp zero cost*. The index is not capnp because it is a **private
cache in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`** that the user is entitled to delete at any moment, is read whole
at startup, and is never exchanged with another process. Capnp's zero-copy advantage is
real when two processes share a mapped message; it is irrelevant when a single process
`read`s 40 MB once and pays nothing. Schema'd, versioned, and a **magic number plus a length**
on the file.

If the ecosystem ever needs a second process to read the index — a `smart-photos-indexd`
daemon, a flatpak-spawned helper, a shared index across two windows — then it becomes a capnp
schema, because at that point two processes *do* map the same message and the zero-copy
argument is real. Recorded here so the decision is a known ratchet rather than an oversight.

### 17.6 What v2 needs to prove before it is admitted

| Candidate | Admission test |
|---|---|
| **RAW decoding** (`libraw` or `rawloader`) | decode a 100-photo RAW corpus in ≤ 3 s wall on 4 cores, with peak RSS ≤ 400 MB, and produce a thumbnail that is visibly equal to the embedded JPEG's. If `rawloader` cannot do it, `libraw` is a C++ build and the answer is a helper process. |
| **Lossy WebP** | `image-webp` is lossless-only today. Either a maintained lossy decoder or the `webp` C library behind the same gate as `libraw`. |
| **AVIF** | decode 100 AVIFs in ≤ 4 s. `ravif` is an *encoder*. Decoding needs a plugin (`libdav1d`) or a pure-Rust port. |
| **Video** | the `ffmpeg-next` link must be optional at build time, with a runtime capability probe and a graceful degrade (§7.12) — a missing FFmpeg must not stop the app from starting. |
| **Face detection** | a model under 8 MB, CPU-only, ≤ 2 s per 1,000 photos, cancellable, pausable, **off by default**, and no GPU requirement. A face feature that needs a working GPU driver is the exact reason an app gets uninstalled. |
| **Colour management** | an ICC transform path that round-trips sRGB ⇄ Display P3 ⇔ Adobe RGB with ΔE < 1. Until then, *Set as Wallpaper* converts to sRGB and says so. |

### 17.7 The `.desktop` file and the file handler

A photo app is not a photo app until the file manager can open a photo with it:
`Type=Application`, `Exec=smart-photos %U`, `Icon=smart-photos`, `StartupNotify=true`,
`DBusActivatable=true`, `Categories=Graphics;PhotoViewer;2DGraphics;RasterGraphics;`, and a
`MimeType` list covering every decodable format in §11.3 plus `video/mp4`, `video/webm`, and
`video/quicktime`.

- `Exec=smart-photos %U` accepts **multiple** URIs and opens them in the viewer in the
  canonical order of the collection they came from, with the rest of the collection navigable.
- `DBusActivatable=true` with a single-instance service, so opening 40 photos from a file
  manager focuses the existing window and adds 40 photos to it rather than starting 40
  processes. **This is not a nicety; it is what makes the app usable from a file manager.**
- `%f` (single file) and `%U` (multiple) are both honoured, and a second instance is refused
  with the request forwarded to the first.

### 18.9 `tests/geometry.rs` — the rects, not the decisions

**Every test above reads a struct. None of them would notice a 2 px vertical offset, a square
button, or two controls that overlap by 3 px. That is the gap this subsection closes, and it is
the single most important test section in this document** — because those three defects are
invisible in a code review, invisible in a unit test, and obvious the instant the window is on
a screen.

**The design that makes it possible: the layout is a pure function, and the painter is a
consumer of its output.**

```rust
/// Every rect the header draws, in one value. Produced before any widget exists.
pub struct BarLayout {
    pub l1: Rect,                 // the bar's own box
    pub l2: Rect,                 // the tab strip
    pub l3: Rect,                 // the content row
    pub leading: Vec<Slot>,       // nav, back, forward, up
    pub title:   Rect,
    pub trailing: Vec<Slot>,      // derived from (view, state)
    pub status:   Option<Rect>,   // the selection count — never focusable
    pub more:     Option<Rect>,   // `None` iff nothing folded, else it is drawn `Unavailable`
}

pub struct Slot { pub cmd: CommandId, pub rect: Rect, pub enabled: bool, pub emphasis: Emphasis }

/// Pure. No widget, no `iced`, no window, no `Task`. This is what the tests call.
pub fn layout(view: &View, state: &BarState, w: f32, h: f32, d: Density) -> BarLayout;
```

**And the one rule that makes these tests worth writing:**

> **`view::bar(...)` may not compute a position. It may only call `layout()` and paint the rects
> it returns. A position computed in the widget layer is a position no test can see, and an
> untestable position is a wrong position.**

`A7-GEOM` asserts this structurally — it greps `src/view/bar.rs` for the forbidden local
geometry, so the coupling cannot rot back into a pile of hand-placed `column![...]` offsets.

**`RECTS` is one flat, comparable value.** `Eq` on `f32` bits is not something to do, so the
harness is:

```rust
fn near(a: Rect, b: Rect, eps: f32) -> bool { /* per-edge |a.x - b.x| <= eps && … */ }
```

with `eps` stated per assertion — **0.5 px for centring, 0.01 px for arithmetic that is supposed
to be exact, and `f32::EPSILON * 4` for the closed-form grid sums of §6.3.** An assertion without
a stated epsilon is not an assertion, it is a hope.

#### The three axes, and why all three

**Every geometry test runs the product of three axes, because the defects only appear where they
cross.** The first draft tested one width and would have shipped all three bugs.

| Axis | Values | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **width** | 320, 360, 480, 600, 840, 1200, 2560 | the fold and the title truncation live here |
| **density** | 1.0, 1.25, 2.0 | `gutter()` and `CONTROL_H` scale, so a rect that is right at 1.0 is wrong at 2.0 |
| **state** | the 4 `BarState`s × 3 views that maximise the cluster | the widest cell is the only one that can overlap |

**7 × 2 × 3 = 42 layouts per assertion, and the whole matrix is built once into a `Vec` and
filtered per assertion** so the cost is one `layout()` call per combination, not 42 calls per
test. **42 layouts × 13 assertions is ~550 rect comparisons, in microseconds.**

#### The assertions, and the defect each one exists to catch

```rust
// C1 — the bar's content is vertically centred. THE bug that motivated this section.
for l in &matrix {
    let row = l.control_row();                       // the union of leading + trailing
    let inner = l.l1.inner(l.note_h());               // after the note line is removed
    assert!(near(row.center_y(), inner.center_y(), 0.5), "at w={} d={}: off by {}",
        l.width(), l.density(), (row.center_y() - inner.center_y()).abs());
}

// C2 — the 20 px glyph and the 16 px title agree, because they are centred together.
for l in &matrix {
    assert!(near(l.title.center_y(), l.control_row().center_y(), 0.5), "…");
}

// C9 — every control is a pill: its height's half IS its radius.
for slot in l.all_slots() {
    assert_eq!(slot.rect.height / 2.0, slot.radius, "{:?} is not a pill", slot.cmd);
}

// C3 — nothing overlaps, anywhere, ever.
for (a, b) in l.all_slots().iter().tuple_combinations() {
    assert!(!a.rect.intersects(b.rect), "{:?} overlaps {:?} at w={}", a.cmd, b.cmd, l.width());
}

// C13 — a derived cluster actually changes the bar's shape.
assert!(l.view_albums_idle.trailing_total() < l.view_folder_idle.trailing_total(),
        "a 3-pill cell and a 1-pill cell drew the same width — the cluster is not derived");
```

**And `C13` is the one that says the rewrite actually happened.** A constant trailing cluster
passes `C1`, `C3`, and `C9` perfectly and fails `C13`, which is the point: **the previous
eleven-command bar would pass almost every geometry test ever written.** The tests that catch it
are `B3`, `B4`, `B5′`, `C13`, and `A7⁗` — the ones that ask *whether the right things are there*,
not whether they are square.

#### What this section deliberately does not do

| Not done | Why |
|---|---|
| **No golden images, no pixel snapshots** | A snapshot of a bar is a picture of the bar, and a person cannot tell from 43 KB of PNG whether the content is 2 px high. **The rects are the truth; a picture of the rects is a liability.** |
| **No headless `iced` render for the header** | The header is 100 % pure layout, so a real render proves nothing the rects do not, and it costs a window, a GPU context, and 40 ms per case. `smart-ui-core` keeps one such test for the gradient angle (`K19`); nothing here needs one. |
| **No assertion on a colour, a font, or a string** | Those are §9's business and belong in `selection`/`keyboard`. This file is about where things *are*. |

**~22 tests, < 250 ms, no display, no fixtures, and every one of them capable of failing for a
reason a person would file a bug about** — which is §18.1's rule, and it is the rule this
subsection is the last word on, because **thousands of tests that cannot see the geometry are
thousands of tests that let a broken bar ship.**

## 0. Mandate

### 0.1 What this is

Smart Photos is a daily-driver photo manager for the folders the user already keeps. It is in
the Smart suite as `AppId::Photos` (`crates/smart-ui-egui/src/shell.rs`), shares the suite's
depth primitives, icons, theme, and appkit settings chrome with Files, and hands back
`Location`s — never private paths — to whatever summoned it.

### 0.2 What this is not

- **Not** a copy-library app. Photos never copies a library the user gave it a path to.
- **Not** an account app. No network connection is ever opened to look at a folder.
- **Not** a native-control app. No stock egui `button`/`slider`/`text_edit` rendering where the
  suite has a drawn primitive; every control is drawn with the suite's depth primitives.
- **Not** a destructive editor. The image's bytes are never overwritten by an adjustment.

### 0.3 Non-negotiable product laws

| # | Law | In one sentence |
|---|-----|-----------------|
| L1 | **Source is truth** | The filesystem the user edits in a file manager is the library. Everything else is a cache that can be deleted. |
| L2 | **No file is ever lost** | Delete is Trash. Permanent delete is typed-confirmed. Both are undoable. |
| L3 | **The image is never touched** | Edits write a sidecar. Pixels are baked only on Export. |
| L4 | **No silent black** | An undecodable file is a declared state with a retry, never a black tile. |
| L5 | **No fake metadata** | Every field in Info is either read from the file/sidecar or labelled with its source. |
| L6 | **One implementation per command** | The bar, the menu, the key, and the palette all dispatch the same `Command`. |
| L7 | **Protocol-first** | The app depends on the protocol, never on a backend. Backends are disposable. |
| L8 | **Reversible AI** | Every AI grouping, suggestion, and auto-tag can be undone to exactly the pre-AI state. |
| L9 | **Honest degrade** | A missing capability (decoder, ffmpeg, MTP) is a stated reason, not a silent gap. |
| L10 | **Bounded everything** | Queues, caches, indexes, and memory are bounded. A 50,000-photo flick is a normal frame. |

### 0.4 The one-sentence test

> *If the user can lose a photo, lose metadata, or be lied to about what they are looking at,
> this spec has failed.*

## 2. Lie hunt

Every lie is stated with its file:line evidence, its severity, and its fix. Severity:
**S1** user-visible falsehood · **S2** silent data loss / staleness · **S3** performance/robustness.

### LIE-1 (S1) — "Actual size" cannot show actual pixels

- **What the UI says:** viewer menu `Actual size` (`photos.rs:597`) and `photos_cmd("actual")` (`:296-301`).
- **What it does:** `zoom = (max(w,h)/700).clamp(1.0, 6.0)` where `w,h` are *already capped* at 1600 px by `photos_load_cur` (`:500`: `if max>1600 resize(1600,1600,Triangle)`). A 6000×4000 photo is displayed at 1600×1067 and "actual size" shows ~2.3× of the *downscaled* bitmap. Pixel-peeping is impossible; the label is false for every photo over 1600 px on its long edge.
- **Also:** `fit` (`zoom=1.0`) is defined as `min(canvas/w, canvas/h).min(1.6)*0.96` in the viewer (`:1051`) — a *third* meaning of "size" that no menu names.
- **Fix (§4, §7):** Full-decode in tiles on demand up to the 250 MP cap (F9 `model/viewer.rs`), zoom 1%–6400% with zoom-to-cursor, named states `Fit/Fill/100/200/300/Free` (F9 `Zoom` enum). `Actual` means 100% of original pixels.

### LIE-2 (S1) — Info panel shows filesystem facts, not photo information

- **Evidence:** `draw_photo_info` (`photos.rs:1294-1324`) lists Name / Dimensions `(preview)` / Size / Kind / Modified / Where / Tags + a 48-bin *luminance* histogram.
- **What's missing:** camera make/model, lens, exposure (f/ISO/shutter), GPS, orientation, software, taken-at source. There is **zero** EXIF code in F1 (verified: `grep -c -i "exif\|orientation" photos.rs` = 0). Orientation is never applied on load, so phone portraits appear sideways and the viewer has no idea why.
- **The label `(preview)` is honest** and must be kept until real dimensions exist — but the panel as a whole is a LIE by omission. The histogram is also *unlabelled* (no axes, no RGB channels, no clipping marks), so it reads as decoration.
- **Fix (§8):** F9 `media.rs` EXIF walk (kamadak-exif on the first 128 KiB, `DateTimeOriginal → Digitized → DateTime`, orientation applied via `oriented()`), `taken_at` with its `TakenSource` sentence, GPS → Places (§6.6), RGB + clipping histogram, srgb/P3 note.

### LIE-3 (S1) — Favorites are a promise that evaporates

- **Evidence:** `favs: HashSet<Location>` in session state (`photos.rs:66`), toggled (`:282-286`), counted in the sidebar (`:673-675`), filtered (`:410`), stored nowhere.
- **Effect:** Every restart, every `#photos` relaunch, every `photos.favs.clear()` — favorites are gone. The heart *feels* permanent; the implementation is a session set. This is the single most trust-breaking lie in the app.
- **Fix (§8):** Persisted favourite flag in the sidecar (`xmp:Rating`-adjacent, F9 XMP pattern) + index flag, written through the undo log (`Body::Flags`). Session set is a cache, never the store.

### LIE-4 (S1) — "Save edited copy" silently transcodes everything to JPEG

- **Evidence:** `photos_save` (`:425-464`) — `to_rgb8()` (alpha dropped), `JpegEncoder::new_with_quality(92)`, `"<stem> edited.jpg"`.
- **Effects:** PNG transparency destroyed; HEIC/AVIF/WebP/TIFF inputs come out as JPEG; EXIF (GPS/camera) stripped; no format/quality choice; no sidecar written; the "non-destructive-feeling editor" header comment (`photos.rs:1-3`) is aspiration, not mechanism. The save is also *not* undoable (no operation recorded).
- **Fix (§7):** Non-destructive sidecar edit + `Export` job (format/quality/scale, `Pictures/Exports/YYYY-MM`, `(Edited)` naming, focus-stealing prevention). The app's own egui editor may keep its JPEG quick-export as an explicitly-labelled *quick* path, never the default mental model.

### LIE-5 (S2) — Desktop Capture video/audio "works" without capturing

- **Evidence:** `capture/mod.rs` `cap_cmd "cap.record"` — `#[cfg(not(target_arch="wasm32"))] let ok = { let _ = &stamp; true };` — native record always succeeds, no stream is opened, `rec_t0` starts, the UI pretends to record. On stop: "Recording saved / Your browser downloaded the file" — on native, nothing was saved anywhere.
- **Fix (§6.10):** Capability probe + honest unavailable state with the reason (`capture.capnp` shaping). A missing backend must not stop the app from starting (F9 §17.6 rule for video).

### LIE-6 (S1) — Kind advertises HEIC/AVIF/TIFF/GIF/WebP that the UI cannot decode

- **Evidence:** `Kind::from_ext` (`model.rs:89`) maps `heic|avif|tif|tiff|gif|webp|ico` → `Kind::Image`. But `smart-ui-egui` depends on `image` with `features = ["png","jpeg"]` only (`Cargo.toml`), and `smart-core` on `["jpeg","png","gif","webp","bmp"]` — **no AVIF, no HEIC, no TIFF, no SVG**. `photos_thumb` / `photos_load_cur` call `image::load_from_memory` which returns `Err` → tile falls to the placeholder icon + `failed.insert()` → the photo is *permanently* black for the session, with no message and no retry (`photos.rs:474-477`).
- **This is the exact failure F9 Appendix C blames for KDE Photos: "HEIC over SMB showing black."** L5 (no silent black) exists to forbid it.
- **Fix (§4.5):** Either ship decoders for every advertised extension or demote the kind to a declared "indexed, preview unavailable — <reason>" state with import/export guidance. The iced spec already takes this position (§2.3: RAW indexed, not decoded; §17.6: AVIF/RAW admission tests). The egui app must take it too.

### LIE-7 (S2) — The ffmpeg video-thumbnail cache never expires

- **Evidence:** `thumbs.rs` very-good `video_thumb`: `key = fnv1a(real_path)`, cache hit = `read(cache).ok()` forever. Replace a video with a different first frame and the thumbnail is stale *permanently*. Same bug class as the missing-mtime LIE in the egui `thumbs HashMap` (keyed by `Location` only, never invalidated).
- **Fix (§4.2):** Cache key **must** include `mtime_ns + size + orientation + edit_generation` (F9 `thumbs.rs::key`, BLAKE3). A key field is there because a stale thumbnail is a permanent visual bug.

### LIE-8 (S3) — "Library size" and counts are computed over a silently truncated scan

- **Evidence:** `photos_scan` budget 6000 (`photos.rs:226-243`): `if budget==0 break` exits only the *inner* `for`; the outer `while` keeps popping dirs and breaking instantly — so the scan *finishes* quickly, reports `scanned=true`, and the sidebar shows "N in library" / "Library size" as if the library were complete. On any real library (>6000 entries under `$HOME`, which includes `.cache`, `target/`, `node_modules`), N is a fiction.
- **Fix (§8):** Roots + ceilings + progress + "12,441 photos · 2,109 skipped" honest counts (F9 `IndexSnapshot` + `ScanPhase`), scan publish every 500, cancellable, partial index kept.

### LIE-9 (S1) — Search implies content search; it is filename-only

- **Evidence:** header placeholder "Search photos" + `photos_list` filename `contains()`. No caption, tag, camera, or EXIF search. Files' Search has a real query language (`search.rs`: `kind:/size:/modified:/tag:` + nucleo fuzzy + cached index + optional content scan). Photos uses none of it.
- **Fix (§9.7, §8):** Faceted query (`Everything/Name/Caption/Tag/Camera`) with a stated `MAX_SCAN` cap and the cap reported in the bar support line (F9 `search.rs`). Reuse the suite engine's ranking discipline.

### LIE-10 (S2) — Albums are folders wearing an album's name

- **Evidence:** sidebar "Albums" section = distinct parent paths (`draw_photos:616-626`), `Album::Folder(f)` filter = `loc.parent()==Some(f)`. Moving a photo out of a folder removes it from its "album" with no notice. No membership editing, no covers, no metadata albums, no smart albums.
- **Fix (§8):** Physical folders stay the library; Albums are metadata membership (F9 §14.3) with covers and reversible AI grouping (§6.5).

### Non-lies that still matter (S3)

- **Rotate/flip are view-only, applied on save.** `rot/flip` mutate only UVs; `photos_save` bakes them. There is no "Apply rotation to file" step, so a user who rotates and saves gets baked pixels with no chance to commit view-only (F9 §7.4 rule: view-only by default, explicit commit).
- **Preset discovery:** preset index is re-derived after slider edits (`draw_photo_edit:1392` — exact `Adjust` equality against `PRESETS`). Any floating-point epsilon creates `usize::MAX` ("custom") silently.
- **Thumbnail budget renders placeholders as final.** Budget 2/frame (`photos_grid:886`, `filmstrip:1213`) with `request_repaint` is correct — but the placeholder (accent wash + `gallery` glyph) has no "loading…" vs "broken" distinction, so a slow library reads as a broken one.
- **Histogram axes:** 48 luminance bars, no R/G/B, no clipping. Decoration, not information (fix in LIE-2).

| Enter → viewer | **≤ 120 ms** | F9 A4. |
| Frame rate | **60 fps**, < 1% dropped through a 50k flick | F9 A3. |
| Editor slider latency | < 16 ms/frame | Target: preview at ≤1024 px on the UI beat (see §4.8). |
| Undo depth | **100 operations** | F9 `undo::DEPTH`. |
| Search scan cap | **50,000** records (reported, not hidden) | F9 `MAX_SCAN`. |

### 4.2 Thumbnail cache — the cache key

Two caches (F9 §2.4/§12.1): a **disk cache** (WebP q82, first frame, deletes freely, 500 MB LRU)
and a **memory cache** (FIFO texture residency, §4.3). The disk cache key is:

```
BLAKE3(abspath ++ 0x00 ++ bucket_px ++ 0x00 ++ mtime_ns ++ 0x00 ++
       orientation ++ 0x00 ++ edit_generation)   → 128-bit hex, fanout 2+2 (256 ways)
```

- **mtime is in the key.** A changed file is a new thumbnail. Any key without mtime is a bug (LIE-7).
- **Orientation is in the key.** EXIF rotation and sidecar rotation bake into the thumbnail (F9 `oriented()`).
- **Edit generation is in the key.** A non-destructive edit changes the *render*, not the file — mtime cannot see it. Every sidecar-edit bumps `smart:EditGeneration` (XMP) and the key changes without touching the image's mtime (F9 test X8).
- **Rung/budget:** the ladder is `[64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096]` on the long edge. `wanted_rung()` never exceeds 1.5× the need ("never larger than 1.5× needed") and re-requests only above a 25% change (`want*4 > have*5`). The 2 hex/2 hex fanout (256 ways) is a `readdir`/`stat` discipline (F9 §12.1).
- **Failure record:** `fail/<digest(abspath,mtime_ns)>` with `FAIL_AFTER = 3`. A file that failed 3 times is skipped with a reason instead of re-probed on every launch (F9 `FailRecord`).

### 4.3 Memory — the big-thumb pool and eviction

- At most **8** above-threshold (≥512 px) decoded thumbs are resident (`big_thumbs 8`). The LRU is by *last-use*, not insert order (F9 grade: FIFO in memory per Shotwell `Caching` note).
- Eviction: when `gpu_budget` or the 8-pool is exceeded, evict the least-recently *seen* rung. The viewer never releases the previous texture before the next upload completes (F9 L6 — no flicker on fast arrowing).
- `TextureHandle`/`egui` upload bandwidth is the scarce resource, not RAM: **≤ 8 uploads/frame**, skipped entirely above 2 px scroll delta.
- `photos_thumb`'s current unbounded `HashMap<Location, (TextureHandle, _)>` (`photos.rs:64`) is retired. Its replacement is the ladder + residency manager above.

### 4.4 Decode pipeline (eiga-pattern, photos-adapted)

1. **Probe first (header only, ≤64 KiB).** `probe_header` reads dimensions without pixels (F9 `media.rs`, F10 `image::image_dimensions`). EXIF walk reads ≤128 KiB on the same handle (F9 `probe_exif`, kamadak-exif).
2. **Reduced-scale decode** where the format offers one (JPEG IDCT-scaled, PNG/WebP downscale). `fast_image_resize` SIMD Lanczos3 in the worker, never on the UI thread.
3. **Priority tiers:** **P0** = the photo being opened + focused cell + selected set (cap 200). **P1** = viewport cells, startup deadline 16 ms / display 100 ms. **P2** = viewport + 1 screen in scroll direction, on 120 ms scroll-idle. **P3** = next 500 in travel direction, whole library when idle. The queue is **rebuilt per scroll direction, not accumulated** (F9 `Queue::rebuild` — a growing queue is the "goes black at 10k per day" bug).
4. **Video stills (eiga reuse):** ffmpeg frame grab at 0.7 s, 384 px, disk-cached (F4-very-good `video_thumb` pattern) — with the §4.2 key (mtime+size), never path-only. ffprobe `MediaInfo` parsing (F8 `source.rs`) is the pattern for the EXIF/container probe.
5. **Broken-file fallback (eiga pattern):** procedural test-card / declared "No preview — <reason> / Retry" tile. Never black (§4.7).

### 4.5 Format honesty (the decoder table)

| Format | Kind | Decode today | Spec |
|--------|------|--------------|------|
| JPEG, PNG | Image | Real (`image` crate) | Real. JPEG IDCT-scaled thumbs. |
| GIF, WebP, BMP | Image | Partial (core decodes, UI crate does not) | **Real or demote** — align UI to core features or demote kind. |
| TIFF | Image | Advertised, not decodable | **Indexed + embedded-preview** until a TIFF decoder is admitted (F9 §17.6 pattern). |
| SVG (Vector) | Vector | Indexed, preview varies | Indexed; resvg render at rung size (F9 dep list). |
| HEIC/HEIF, AVIF | Image | Advertised, not decodable (LIE-6) | **Indexed, preview via embedded thumbnail or declared-unavailable**, admission test §17.6 before full decode. |
| RAW (CR2/CR3/NEF/ARW/DNG/ORF/RW2/RAF/PEF/SRW/X3F/3FR/FFF/RWL) | *missing* (F1: `Other`) | Invisible to scan | **Kind::Raw, indexed + embedded JPEG preview** (F9 `Kind::Raw` + §2.3: indexed, not decoded). Full decode only after the §17.6 admission test. |
| JXL, QOI, TGA, ICO, PPM/PGM/PNM/PAM, FF, JFIF | *missing* (F1) | `Other` | **Kind::Image** (F9 `from_extension` — adopt verbatim). |
| Video (MP4/MKV/WebM/MOV/AVI/M4V/MPG/MPEG) | Video | Eiga only | **Kind::Video in Photos** with ffmpeg stills (§4.4) + capture-frame. |

Every demoted kind is a *declared* state ("Indexed — preview unavailable: <reason>"), never a black tile.

### 4.6 What is measured, and when it is a failure (perf tests)

F9 `tests/perf.rs` (P1–P7) + `tests/geometry.rs` (G1–G36) are adopted as the acceptance suite
for this section: RSS, built-range invariance, O(1) row lookup, allocation ceilings, **no
`fs::metadata`/`read_dir`/`File::open`/`decode` in `views/`** (P5 — a source grep), **no HTTP
client in the resolved graph** (P6 — a graph grep), cold-load timing. A regression is a line of
code, and a test that greps for that line cannot be defeated by a rewrite elsewhere.

### 4.7 Placeholders, broken tiles, and the no-silent-black rule

Three distinct visuals, never merged:

| State | Visual | Meaning |
|-------|--------|---------|
| **Loading** | Skeleton (accent wash) + shimmer, exactly 3 skeleton variants (F9 §16.1) | Requested, in queue. Distinct from broken. |
| **Indexed, no preview** | Dueduo glyph + reason text ("No preview — HEIC decoder unavailable") | Demoted kind (§4.5). Has a "Why?" affordance. |
| **Broken** | `gallery` glyph + "Could not open that image" + Retry | `load_from_memory` failed on a decodable kind. `failed` is a *retryable* set with backoff, not permanent. |

### 4.8 Editor performance (the slider rule)

- Slider edits preview on a **≤1024 px proxy** in the same frame (< 16 ms); the full-res
  `process()` runs debounced (800 ms, F9 §13.6) in a worker and the texture swaps when ready.
- The current egui `process()` is O(w·h) over a *1600 px-capped* source on the UI thread
  (`photos.rs:152-191`, `photos_reprocess:526-532`) — fine at proxy size, a jank source at
  full size. It moves off the UI beat per the rule above.
- Preset previews stay 120 px live thumbs (already correct in F1).

## 5. Protocol-first architecture

### 5.1 The rule

> **The app depends on the protocol. Backends are disposable. No code path in Photos may open
> a file, a device, or a network socket directly.**

Concretely: Photos today depends on `smart_core::{Vfs, Location, Entry, Kind, Registry,
Library}` directly (F1 `use smart_core::*;`). That is *already* the right dependency direction
(panel: a storage abstraction + registry), but it must be **re-targeted onto the Cap'n Proto
contract** so a Linux, Android, and iOS backend can be swapped without recompiling the UI.

### 5.2 Domain mapping (Photos → `smart-protocol-rs`)

| Photos need | Protocol domain | Contract |
|-------------|-----------------|----------|
| List / stat / read / write / rename / mkdir / watch a directory | `domain-files` (`files.capnp`) | `listDirectory` (paginated filter), `statFile`, `openFile/readFile` (bounded `DataHandle` pulls), `watchDirectory` (pull+cancel), `getFileMetadata`, `compareFiles`. |
| Photo library as content-addressed media | `domain-media` (`media.capnp`) | `MediaItem` (`contentHash`, so a photo is addressable by bytes), `MediaMetadata.aiTags` for object/face tags (§6.4), `getSupportedFormats`/`transcode` for export (§7.5), `SharePreview` (thumbnail+title for links). |
| Browse drives / SD / USB volumes Photos scans | `domain-storage` (`storage.capnp` + `mount.capnp`) | `listDevices`/`listVolumes` for removable sources; `capacity` via `getDiskUsage`. Pool/SMART/Snapshot surface is **not** Photos' surface — Photos never partitions, raids, or snapshots; it *reads* volumes. |
| Capture (camera + screen) | `camera.capnp` + `capture.capnp` | `capturePhoto` (`PhotoOptions` + `HdrOptions` + `CaptureFilter`), `detectFaces`/`detectScene` (§6.4), `getRichMetadata` (EXIF-rich capture record), `privacyMask`. Screen capture rides the same `Frame` envelope (`capture.capnp`). |
| Location → Places / on-map | `location.capnp` | `LocationRef` (embeddable in the photo record), `getHistory` (paginated), `PrivacyLevel` (user-controlled granularity). The Places *map itself is offline* (§6.6) — the protocol carries coordinates, never tiles. |
| Offline sync + backup (photo library) | `backup.capnp` | `createBackup` (full/incremental/differential), `listBackups`, `restoreBackup`, `syncToRemote` with `resumeToken` (interrupted syncs resume, never restart). Progress via subscription, never poll loops. |
| Search index (shared, cached) | `system_search.capnp` + `runtime_search.capnp` | Photos' query surface (§9.7) is a client of the shared index; the 50k cap is the client's discipline, not the protocol's. |
| Trash / versions / restore | `files.capnp` (`getFileVersions`, `restoreVersion`) | Trash semantics (§9.4) map to versioned remove + `files` trash. |
| Capabilities / auth | `capability.capnp` | Holding a reference *is* authority (the `BlockProvider` precedent in `storage.capnp`). No per-method tokens. |

### 5.3 Backend obligations (disposable backends)

| Backend | Must provide | Degrade rule |
|---------|--------------|--------------|
| Linux (desktop) | `files` over the local VFS + `trash` crate + `notify` watch + ffmpeg (optional, probed) | No ffmpeg → video stills become declared-unavailable; still-image pipeline unaffected. |
| Android | `files` over ADB/MTP (§6.9) + scoped-storage media store | No ADB → phone source absent (stated), library unaffected. |
| iOS | `files` over PhotoKit bridge + `FileManager` | No PhotoKit → flat file sources only (stated). |

Hadron note: the app is **target-agnostic**. `THREADED` (F4 `exec.rs`) already encodes the
wasm rule (worker threads native, inline in browser). Every §5 call is pull/push with a bound —
a wasm build never blocks a frame on a >token read.

### 5.4 What must be removed (direct-backend couplings)

- `photos.rs` `be.read_bytes(&l, 24MB)` / `48MB` full-file reads (`:474`, `:493`) → bounded
  `DataHandle` pulls sized by the rung (proxy first, full only on zoom).
- `photos_save`'s `create_file` + direct `write` → `createFile` with parents + conflict policy
  (`overwrite: u8` already in very-good `Settings` — adopt it).
- `photos_scan`'s recursive `fs.list` walk → `walkTree` (paginated, max-depth) with progress +
  cancellation.
- Thumb `read(&loc.path, 48MB)` (F4 `thumbs.rs:31`) → probe-once, then ranged reads.

## 6. New ideas — the unknown unknowns

Each entry is numbered, motivated by a lie or a gap above, and classified **P0** (ship blocker)
/ **P1** (should ship) / **P2** (designed, admit later with a gate).

### 6.1 Duplicate finder (content-based) — P1

- **Gap:** `analyze.rs` duplicates are name-pattern only (`copy_original`: `"Report (1).pdf"`,
  `" - Copy"`, `"_copy"`). Two identical `IMG_0001.jpg` in different folders are invisible.
- **Design:** Two-phase (F9 §11.2): cheap listing → `hash256k` (BLAKE3 over the first 256 KiB —
  F9 `hash_prefix` option) → full BLAKE3 confirm on candidates → perceptual hash for
  near-duplicates (re-encoded/cropped copies). Reuse `analyze::Scan` + `JunkKind::Duplicates`
  (Safety::Review — *your* call, never pre-selected). The sidebar "Duplicates" surface (F9 §5.6)
  shows the review set (2.4 MB / 4 files dynamic) with **Keep both / Keep newest / Keep best**
  and per-item **Undo**.
- **Protocol:** `files.capnp` `storeContentAddressed` / `getByHash` / `deduplicate` — the
  content-addressed store *is* the dedup primitive. `media.capnp` `MediaItem.contentHash`
  makes it cross-backend.

### 6.2 Offline sync (library state sync) — P1

- **Gap:** Favorites/tags/albums/ratings live in exactly one place (or, in F1, nowhere durable).
- **Design:** The index + XMP sidecars are the sync payload; device-local state (pane width,
  zoom, settings) never syncs. Sync state carries a caller-chosen `resumeToken` (`backup.capnp`
  precedent) so an interrupted sync resumes. Conflict rule: sidecar wins for *metadata*,
  filesystem wins for *bytes*; both sides always offer Undo. Offline-first: every sync
  affordance works with the network absent, and "Sync" is a *backup*, never a gate on browsing.

### 6.3 Backup integration (photo-library backup) — P1

- **Gap:** Photos has no backup path. `backup.capnp` is complete and unused.
- **Design:** "Back up library" over `BackupService.createBackup` (full/incremental, encrypted
  first-class), schedule (`getSchedule`/`setSchedule`), verify (callable — the batch's fix that
  made integrity checking *reachable*), restore with progress subscription. Estimate before
  creating (`getEstimatedSize`). The library's "Library size" card (already in the sidebar)
  gains a "Backed up · 2 days ago / Never" line.

### 6.4 Face detection & object search — P2 (admission-gated)

- **Gap:** `camera.capnp` `detectFaces`/`detectScene` + `MediaMetadata.aiTags` exist; Photos
  exposes neither. The assistant's "Make this photo warmer" suggestions (F2) are prompt theatre.
- **Design (the gate, F9 §17.6):** a model **under 8 MB, CPU-only, ≤ 2 s per 1,000 photos,
  cancellable, pausable, off by default**, no GPU requirement. Until a candidate passes the
  gate, "People" is an *empty state with the plan stated*, never a fake list. When admitted:
  face thumbnails + per-person albums, object chips (`dog`, `sunset`, `receipt`), all stored as
  `MediaItem` `aiTags` + XMP `PersonInImage`, all indexed in the §9.7 Query (`camera:` today,
  `tag:`/`object:`/`person:` as facets).

### 6.5 Smart albums + AI grouping (reversible) — P1

- **Gap:** Albums are folders (LIE-10). No smart albums, no grouping.
- **Design:** Smart albums = saved queries over the §9.7 surface: `kind:raw`, `gps:here`,
  `aesthetic:low` (blur/dark/duplicate clusters), `scene:beach` (post-§6.4). AI grouping
  ("This week", "Hiking trip", "Duplicates to review") is a *suggestion with a preview, an
  Apply, and a Dismiss* — and **every Apply is one Undo to the pre-AI state** (L8). Grouping
  writes membership only; it never moves a byte. Rating (`Ctrl+0…5`) and tag rename are atomic
  across the library with a single undo (F9 §14.1/§14.2 laws).

### 6.6 Locations / on-map (offline) — P1

- **Gap:** No GPS is read, no map exists. `location.capnp` is complete and unused.
- **Design (F9 `places.rs`, adopted verbatim as behaviour):** GPS is clustered into ~2.5 km
  cells (`Cell2::of`, deterministic — same coordinate, same cell, every rescan). The Places
  section is a lazy tree; past 8 cells a leaf shows a **map strip**. **The map has no basemap
  and leaks nothing:** a vector graticule (0.1° step) + density heat + photo markers. No tile
  is downloaded, no geocoder is called. Unplaced photos are a visible leaf at the bottom of the
  section (a hole in a tree is not discoverable). `PrivacyLevel` governs export: `exact`/`fine`/
  `coarse` (city-level) / `none` (strip on share). EXIF GPS → `LocationRef` in the record.

### 6.7 Recents tombstones — P1

- **Gap (verified):** `Library::touch_recent` dedups by `Location` equality and truncates to 60
  (`library.rs:155-159`). A deleted file it points at stays until 60 *newer* recents evict it —
  there is no existence check, no missing state, no purge. The Files Recents surface renders a
  row for a file that no longer exists.
- **Design:** Recents entries gain `available: bool` + `missing_since`. A watch event or a
  failed `statFile` marks the entry; the UI renders Missing ("This photo moved or was deleted —
  [Relink] [Dismiss]") and **never silently deletes the record** (F9 I8 law: missing ≠ gone,
  "comes back when the file returns"). Purge at 90 days missing, dim at 30 (F9 §11.8). Same
  treatment for pins and tag assignments (`rekey()` already survives rename; a *delete* needs
  the tombstone).

### 6.8 MTP / phone import (the file-manager phone bug, fixed) — P0

- **The bug (verified):** `devices.rs` implements `adb` (`AdbVfs`, `adb:` provider, battery
  level, `/sdcard`) — and **nothing else for phones**. There is no MTP/PTP provider
  (`libgphoto2`/`gvfs`). A phone plugged in as MTP ("File transfer") is invisible to Files;
  a fortiori invisible to Photos: `photos_scan` starts at `be.home()` and never enumerates
  `adb:*`, USB mass-storage volumes, or SD cards. **"File manager phone never mounts" is not a
  metaphor — it is the code.**
- **Fix:** (a) MTP provider (gvfs/libgphoto2 on Linux; PhotoKit on iOS; Android MTP via ADB or
  the system media provider) registered in the `Registry` like `AdbVfs`; (b) Photos imports
  via `watchDirectory`-style monitoring of the device + **Import** action (new-file detection by
  `contentHash`, RAW+JPEG pairs (§6.9), SD-card `DCIM/` handling); (c) Sources are
  `read_only + removable` (F9 `Source` type): no in-place mutation, explicit "Copy to library".
- **Acceptance:** plug → appears in Files devices **and** Photos sources without a restart;
  `DCIM` contents appear in the timeline; safe-eject is honored.

### 6.9 RAW + HDR stack — P1

- **Gap:** No RAW kind, no stacking, no HDR. `camera.capnp` has `HdrOptions` (bracket
  capture + merge strategy) and `PhotoOptions` declares `hdr`; Photos ignores both.
- **Design:** RAW files are `Kind::Raw` (§4.5), indexed with embedded-JPEG preview, EXIF-probed
  (camera/lens/exposure/GPS all present in RAW EXIF), grouped into stacks (`IMG_0001.CR2` +
  `IMG_0001.JPG` = one tile, `Stack` badge). HDR = a photo entity with N bracket members +
  a merge recipe (sidecar); the merged result is an Export (§7.5), never a replacement. Until
  a RAW decoder passes the §17.6 gate (100-photo corpus ≤ 3 s, ≤ 400 MB RSS, thumbnail visibly
  equal to embedded JPEG), decoding is *embedded preview only* — stated, not faked.

### 6.10 Capture (camera + screen, protocol-shaped) — P1

- **Gap:** Desktop Capture exists (screenshot → Pictures, visible in Photos immediately — real),
  but native video/audio record is a stub (LIE-5) and the camera is untouched.
- **Design:** 
  - **Camera:** `capturePhoto` with `PhotoOptions` (format, HDR, filter chain, watermark),
    `setZoom`/`setFlash`/`setFocus`/`setExposureCompensation`, `getRichMetadata` for the
    capture record (all orientation-correct at capture time, never after).
  - **Screen:** keep the working screenshot path (Screen/Window/Region + countdown + clipboard);
    fix record with a capability probe + `capture.capnp` `FrameStream` — a missing backend is
    an honest "Recording isn't available here — <reason>", never a fake success.
  - **Ingest:** every capture lands in `Pictures` (or the Photos capture album) and is
    `contentHash`-indexed like any other photo. The Capture recent list (`capture/mod.rs`
    right column) clicks through to Photos (already does — keep).

### 6.11 Palette — P2 (with a hard rule)

- **Rule:** "Palette" in this spec = **colour-histogram palette** (extracted dominant colours /
  film-strip palette per photo or album), *not* the command palette. Confusing the two in UI
  copy is forbidden.
- **Design:** per-photo palette (5 swatches from the 40×40 quantized thumb — F9 `Photo::dominant`
  already stores it), copy-as-CSS/hex, "Find similar colour" (a facet over dominant), album
  palette strip. The **command** palette stays `Ctrl+K` (already wired in `photos_library_menu`).

### 6.12 Print / Share / Export surfaces — P1

- **Gap:** No print, no share sheet, no export-as. The menus offer wallpaper + copy-path and
  stop. Command index (F9 Appendix A) lists them; this build has none.
- **Design:** Print (1×, 4-up, 9-up layouts, EXIF-orient respected), Share via portal
  (`media.capnp` `SharePreview` — thumbnail, title, GPS-strip per `PrivacyLevel`), Export-as
  (`Ctrl+S`-equivalent: format/quality/scale, §7.5), Copy as markdown link. Every surface
  carries the same availability derivation (§9.8 — computed, not declared).

### 6.13 Light table (compare) — P1

- **Gap:** Single-photo hold-compare exists (real). Multi-compare does not.
- **Design:** F9 §7.9 compare (light table): 2–8 photos side by side, synchronized
  zoom/pan, per-photo info on hover. Reuses the filmstrip + viewer zoom model. Availability:
  `≥2, uniform kind`.

### 6.14 Screenshots heuristic + screen recordings — P2

- F9 §5.5: long-edge ≥ 2000 px + ratio 1.6–2.4 → "Screenshots" collection (Capture output
  auto-files here). Screen recordings (Capture mode 1) are `Kind::Video` with stills (§4.4) and

## 7. Editor (non-destructive, sidecar-backed, reversible)

### 7.1 The law

> **The image's bytes never change.** An edit is a sidecar write. Pixels are baked only on
> Export, and Export names the file so no one mistakes it for the original.

This replaces the egui "save edited copy" model (LIE-4) and completes the iced command surface
(`Crop`/`Adjust`/`Edit`/`ResetEdits` are declared in F9 `msg.rs` but `apply_edit` handles only
metadata — this section is the pixel editor those commands point at).

### 7.2 The sidecar

- Location: `.jpg.xmp` (`dng`) default on write, `.xmp` (`lr`) read — F9 `xmp.rs` (`SidecarMode`,
  `candidates()`, `existing()`). Both are read; `dng` wins writes.
- **Eight owned elements** (F9 `OWNED`, 9 with generation — the count is asserted by test because
  a ninth is a decision): `xmp:Rating`, `dc:title`, `dc:description`, `lr:hierarchicalSubject`,
  `tiff:Orientation`, `exif:GPSLatitude`, `exif:GPSLongitude`, `Iptc4xmpCore:PersonInImage`,
  `smart:EditGeneration` + the `smart:` adjustment/crop parameter packet. **No `xmpMM:DerivedFrom`
  is ever written** (darktable interop — F9 §13.2).
- **Read-modify-write preserves foreign elements byte-for-byte** (F9 test X1 with a 20-element
  foreign fixture). Losing another application's metadata is the worst bug a non-destructive
  editor has.
- A malformed sidecar degrades to "no sidecar," never an error (F9 X6). A write to a read-only
  source fails with the reason, not a panic, not silence (F9 X9).

### 7.3 What the editor can do (every op reversible)

| Op | Reversibility | Notes |
|----|---------------|-------|
| **Crop** (rect + aspect presets 1:1/4:3/3:2/16:9/4:5 + free) | Sidecar rect + undo | Aspect-locked by default; the crop *is* the render transform, so it participates in the thumb key via edit generation. |
| **Rotate** (90°×N) + **Flip H/V** | Sidecar `tiff:Orientation` + view-only default + explicit **Apply rotation to file** (touches, confirmed) | View-only by default (F9 §7.4). Applying writes the file and is itself undoable (before-image). |
| **Adjust** (Exposure/Contrast/Saturation/Warmth/Vignette + Blacks/Whites/Clarity/Texture/Dehaze) | Sidecar params + undo | The egui 5-slider `process()` math is the starting point (§4.8 proxy rule). Presets (F1's 8) become named recipes with the same values. |
| **Filters** (8 presets + custom) | Sidecar recipe + undo | Live 120 px previews (already real in F1). |
| **Caption / Title / People / Tags / Rating** | Sidecar + undo | `apply_edit` today (F9) — kept, wired through the same log. |
| **Reset all edits** | One undo to the pre-reset state | `ResetEdits` command; not a file rewrite. |

### 7.4 History (the operation log)

- `undo.rs` pattern, adopted verbatim: an `Operation` records the **before image + the forward
  path**, never a bespoke inverse. `Undo` depth **100**. The log is a *user-visible* surface
  (last 20, labelled in the user's words — F9 `history()`) because "a safety feature the user
  cannot see is a safety feature nobody believes."
- Every Edit / Tag / Rate / Favourite / Move / Trash / Export / Rotation-commit pushes one
  operation. Undo writes the before-image back through the **same** path that produced it
  (sidecar write, trash restore, export-file removal). There is no second code path (F9 §16.3;
  the `LogAdapter` stub in `undo.rs` is deleted — the real trait impl must keep `can_undo/redo`
  and history truthful; a stub that answers `false` is LIE-5's cousin).

### 7.5 Export — where pixels are allowed

- Triggered only by `Export` / `Export as`. Format (JPEG q82 default, PNG, WebP), quality, scale
  (long-edge), **location**: `Pictures/Exports/YYYY-MM`, **naming**: `<name> (Edited).<ext>`
  with `Rename` default on collision (never overwrite — F9 §13.5 law). The export is an undoable
  operation (its `written` files are recorded; undo removes exactly those).
- `Set as Wallpaper` converts to sRGB first and **says so** (F9 §17.6 colour-management staging:
  until an ICC path round-trips ΔE < 1, wallpaper conversion is labelled).

### 7.6 The editor surface

A side panel (480 px at ≥1200 px width, else full) per F9 §13.4: header with **Hold: original**
(hold `\` or the button) + **Reset**; FILTERS 4-up grid with live previews; ADJUST slider stack
(track 28, knob 20, `radius.full`, double-click = reset one); the slider shows its *numeric
value* (F1 does `±100` — keep). All motion respects `reduced_motion` (§9.1).

## 8. Data model, index, XMP, tombstones

### 8.1 Photo identity

- **`PhotoId = first 16 bytes of BLAKE3(dev ∪ inode)`** (F9 `model.rs::photo_id`). The **path
  is excluded** — a rename keeps its identity (F9 test I9). Zeros still hash (a missing file
  keeps its identity when it returns — a rename-in). Rename keeps album membership. The
  egui `Location` (`fs:path`) remains the *address*; `PhotoId` is the *identity*. Both are
  carried; rekeying (`library.rs::rekey`, prefix match) is kept as the address migration.

### 8.2 Classification (adopt F9 `from_extension` verbatim)

`Image | Video | Raw` (F9) over the egui `Kind` superset: JPEG/JFIF/PNG/WebP/GIF/BMP/TIFF/TIF/AVIF/
JXL/QOI/TGA/ICO/PPM/PGM/PNM/PAM/FF/HEIC/HEIF/SVG + video (MP4/MKV/WebM/MOV/AVI/M4V/MPG/MPEG) +
RAW (CR2/CR3/NEF/ARW/DNG/ORF/RW2/RAF/PEF/SRW/X3F/3FR/FFF/RWL/RAW). `.xmp` is **never**
indexed as a photo (it binds to its base image — F9 `classify`/`sidecar_base`).

### 8.3 `taken_at`, resolved once, with its source stored

Order (F9 `scan::probe`): **EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` → `DateTimeDigitized` → `DateTime` →
four filename shapes only → container creation time → mtime → Unknown (badged, never guessed)**.
The four shapes (§11.4): `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`, `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH.MM.SS`,
`YYYY-MM-DD`. A general date-from-string is how a library fills up with photographs from 2001
(from the digit `2`). The info panel shows the sentence: `EXIF / filename / container /
file modified time / unknown` (F9 `TakenSource::sentence`). The day boundary is a user setting
(`day_starts_at_04`, default off — Shotwell migrants see their grouping explained, not argued
with). Moments: 3 h gap (1/3/6/12 configurable), 2 s burst window.

### 8.4 Orientation

EXIF orientation → sidecar orientation wins → file dims are `oriented()` (F9 `media.rs`) so the
cell aspect, the thumbnail bake, and the viewer fit all agree. 5–8 swap width/height. This
single function retires the "sideways phone photos" bug (LIE-2).

### 8.5 The index (binary cache, self-healing)

- One file, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/<app>/index.v1`, `SMPHOTOS` magic + version + count + records,
  ~400 B/record (100k ≈ 40 MB, read ≈ 40 ms — F9 §2.1). **Not Cap'n Proto** by decision (single
  process, `read` once, never memory-mapped across processes); it becomes Cap'n Proto if a
  second process ever maps it (F9 §17.4 — the ratchet is recorded).
- **Corrupt index = missing index**: unlinked and rebuilt, no user-visible error (F9
  `load_from`). **Validated against `stat`** for every record on load (I11). Per-file mtime
  change invalidates exactly that record + one thumb key (I7). `rm -rf` the cache → identical
  `PhotoId`s on rescan (I6).
- Scan publishes every 500 items, depth ≤ 64, no symlink follow, hidden skipped
  (`Pictures/.thumbnails` is not the user's photographs), per-root ceiling 4,000,000, EXIF bound
  128 KiB, header 64 KiB, hash prefix 256 KiB (F9 `index.rs` consts). Cancelling keeps the
  partial index (I14).

### 8.6 Missing, watch, and the always-live library

- Delete event → `available: false`, record **kept** (I8). `missing_since` set; dim at 30 d,
  purge at 90 d. Bringing the file back restores the record (I16 analogue).
- Live watching (`notify` debouncer) → index deltas, never full rescans. Rescan (`Ctrl+R`) is
  manual and cancellable.
- `has_device()` / sources: `/photos` (non-removable, watched) + any removable (§6.8) +
  `adb:`/`MTP` phone sources. Sources carry `read_only` + `removable` + `watched` + `last_count`.

### 8.7 Records carry

`Photo { id, path, source, name, kind, size, mtime_ns, dims (oriented), taken_at + source,
rating, favourite, tags[], caption, title, gps (lat,lon,alt), camera (make,model), dominant
(swatch), hash256k, available, missing_since, edit_generation }` — F9 `index.rs::encode` packs
exactly this. No field without a consumer.

## 9. UX — accessibility, drag-drop, picker, trash, dialogs, settings

### 9.1 Accessibility

| Concern | Rule |
|---------|------|
| Keyboard completeness | Every command has a key **or** a discoverable menu path (F9 K9). No key is bound twice (K8). Grid: arrows move by 1 / `cols`, `PgUp/PgDn` preserve column, `Ctrl+Arrow` moves focus without touching selection, `Shift+Arrow` extends (§6.6). Viewer: `1/2/3` = 100/200/300, `Ctrl+Arrow` never enters selection. `Esc` in viewer returns focus to the originating cell (K7). |
| Focus visibility | A focus ring (2 px / 3 px in high contrast) on every focusable control, inset 2 px out of the gutter. The focused **and** selected cell has exactly one 2 px edge (G18). Focus order is derived from layout (F9 §4.10), never hand-listed. |
| Screen reader | Every icon control has a label; every dialog announces its title and its destructive consequence; toasts announce. `Unavailable` changes ink, never alpha (G19). |
| Motion | `reduced_motion` disables springs, crossfade, and Ken Burns (the spring helpers take the flag). |
| Contrast & type | High-contrast toggle + text-scale slider (Settings → Appearance), both live. No two roles share a size; nothing under 12 px; chrome ≤ 18 px (G23). `Unavailable` ink survives HC (G19). |
| Targets | ≥ 44 px desktop / 40 px phone per control (F9 `target()`). Current hearts 30 px / tools 34 px / filmstrip thumbs 62×54 grow or gain padding to meet the target without changing the visual (hit-rect > paint-rect). |
| Colour independence | State is never colour-only: selection = 2 px border, favourite = filled heart, missing = hatch + label, loading = skeleton + shimmer. |

### 9.2 Drag & drop

- **Into Photos:** image files dropped into the grid → Import (content-hash dedup, RAW+JPEG
  pairing, "Imported N, skipped M duplicates"). Dropped into the viewer → open the first,
  queue the rest. Dropped onto a folder in the sidebar → Move/Copy with the same collision rule
  as everywhere (`<name> (2).ext`, toast names the count). The OS drag preview never fights the
  filmstrip's own drag-scroll (F9 G20: every drag rect is disjoint from every icon-button rect).
- **Out of Photos:** drag a cell → the `Location` (or exported temp file for edited renders)
  leaves as `text/uri-list` + `image/png`. This is the eiga `eiga_drop` pattern (`DroppedFileHandle`
  → `eiga_open` + subtitle-track branch) mirrored: native decodes for real; wasm states the
  reason instead of pretending (`File drops open real videos in the desktop app` — keep the
  honesty, fix the capability).
- **Trash drop:** dropping onto the sidebar Trash row = Trash (undoable, never asks). Dropping
  onto Files = same. `clear_drop_targets` discipline (shell already does this per-frame) is kept.

### 9.3 Picker (with New Folder / search / multi-select)

The wallpaper picker (`picker.rs`, desktop variant) is promoted to the generic **system picker**:
`PickPurpose ∈ {Wallpaper, Open, Save, Import}` + an optional format filter. It keeps: places
rail (first 10), breadcrumb with enclosing-folder, grid with folder + image cells, footer with
selection name + size, `Choose`/`Cancel`/`Enter`. It **gains**:

| Capability | Behaviour |
|------------|-----------|
| **New Folder** | `New Folder` button in the header (+ `Ctrl+Shift+N`): inline name entry in the current directory, created via `createDirectory(parents:false)`, failures inline ("A folder by that name exists"). Enabled only when the current dir is writable (`is_writable()`); on read-only sources the button is `Unavailable` with the reason. |
| **Search** | Two modes, labelled: *In this folder* (current, substring) and *Everywhere* (recursive `walkTree` / shared index, capped + reported per §6.2). Esc clears. The search box shows its scope in the hint text. |
| **Multi-select** | `Ctrl+click` toggles, `Shift+click` ranges; footer shows "N selected · M MB" and `Choose N`. The wallpaper purpose stays single-select (availability derives from purpose). |
| **Sort** | Name / Date / Size (same `sort_entries` as Files). |
| **Hidden toggle** | A "Show hidden" switch; hidden `Pictures/.thumbnails` stays out by default. |
| **Formats** | A filter row (All / JPEG / PNG / HEIC / RAW / Video) driven by §4.5 kinds; demoted kinds are listed with their reason, never hidden silently. |
| **Preview** | Hover shows a 256 px preview (existing thumb ladder rung, no full decode). |

### 9.4 Trash integration

- Photos gains the full Files trash surface (reusing `ops::Trash` + the `trash` crate +
  `trash_restore` `.trashinfo` path — F3 backend already has all three):
  - **Move to Trash** (`Delete`): undoable, no confirmation, toast with **Undo** (F9 `ToastKind::Undo`).
  - **Delete permanently** (`Shift+Delete`): **typed confirmation** — the dialog asks the user to type `delete` (§9.5). Only in the photos viewer's Delete group; never on the main grid path.
  - **Restore**: from the Trash collection; restores to the recorded original path, recreating parents, toast naming what was restored.
  - **Empty Trash**: shows count + total size, typed-confirm when > 1 GiB (F9 §11.10 `trash badge > 1 GiB`).
  - Missing records in the library stay tombstoned (§8.6) until restored or purged — Trash and Missing are different concepts and the UI never merges them.

### 9.5 Destructive dialogs (the confirmation that earns its place)

- **Trash is never confirmed.** It is undoable. A dialog there is friction without safety.
- **Permanent delete** is typed (`delete` — F9 §16.4). The dialog names the count and the size,
  the **first** item (when N>1), and the fact that the files do not come back. `confirm_delete`
  setting (already in `Settings`, F3) governs *Files'* permanent deletes; Photos reuses the same
  toggle and the same `m_confirm` component (`modals.rs:757`).
- **Clear metadata** / **Apply rotation** / **Empty Trash > 1 GiB** each carry their own typed-or-
  confirmed dialog with the rule *destructive ⇒ undoable ⇒ typed-confirmed or both* (F9 A20).
- **Read-only sources** never reach a destructive dialog: the command is `Unavailable` with the
  reason ("This device is read-only" — F9 `Source::Sentence`).

### 9.6 Settings — the file-manager-only style (kept, completed)

- **Style kept:** Photos settings use the shared `draw_app_settings(ui, win, AppId::Photos, pages,
  rows_for) → Option<(page,row,SVal)>` (F1 `photos_settings:1406`, F6 appkit `draw_app_settings`).
  Pages are icon+label (`tuning-2 General / play Viewer / gallery Library`), rows are
  `SRow::Choice/Toggle/Slider/Button` with icon + label + sub + typed `SVal`. No Photos-only
  settings chrome is introduced.
- **Persistence fixed:** today's Photos rows (sort, fill, captions, tile, gap, slide_secs,
  filmstrip, tools, wheel_zoom, Rescan/Clear-favorites/Reset-thumbs) are **session-only** and
  evaporate. They persist to the user settings TOML (F9 `settings.rs` pattern: per-user file,
  **unknown-key preservation** so a downgrade loses nothing, `density`/`text_scale`/
  `high_contrast`/`reduced_motion` surfaced here as well as in the OS Settings app).
- **Pages (canonical):** General (d Density, text scale, high contrast, reduced motion, sort,
  thumbnails Fill/Fit, captions, tile size, grid spacing), Viewer (slideshow interval, filmstrip,
  tool bar, scroll-to-zoom, info panel default, day-boundary + moment gap), Library (roots to
  scan + depth + hidden, sidecar mode dng/lr, Reset index, Reset thumbnails, **Export settings**).
  Every row is a `SRow` in the file-manager style; the style is the contract.

### 9.7 Search (query surface, not a box)

The header search (F1 toolbar capsule) becomes a **faceted query**: free text + an optional
field filter (`Everything | Name | Caption | Tag | Camera` — F9 `Field`), case-insensitive,
**capped at 50,000 records with the cap stated in the support line** (F9 `MAX_SCAN` — a query
that would read every field of every record says so instead of scanning). Ranking reuses the
suite engine's discipline (exact filters, fuzzy terms, cached index); the Photos client owns the
cap and the report. Search results keep **viewer order = grid order** (F9 G36).

### 9.8 Command discipline (one implementation per command)

Every command is a `Command` id (Appendix A) dispatched from exactly four surfaces — bar, menu,
key, palette — and **one implementation**. Availability is *derived* from the selection and the
source (`Holding / Uniform / Touches / Viewer / Unavailable`), never declared per-surface
(F9 §8.6). A test asserts the table: no id bound to two keys (K8), every command reachable
(K9), bar never shows more than 4 leading + 3 trailing (A7).
